title: Top Biopharma Analyst Sees Biotech M&A Market Reopening After a Long Freeze
excerpt: A top Barclays biopharma analyst says the forces that froze biotech dealmaking are breaking apart, and the pharma giants shopping for acquisitions have very...
content_html:
Quick Read

  • Moderna and Merck's cancer vaccine cut melanoma recurrence risk 49%, sending MRNA up 177% on readout day and 392% year to date.

  • Revolution Medicines' daraxonrasib nearly doubled pancreatic cancer survival versus chemo, with RVMD surging 163% year to date on a $45 billion market cap.

  • AbbVie announced a $10.9 billion Apogee deal and still pledged more M&A capacity as Humira sales collapsed 36% to $756 million.

Barclays' Emily Field, Head of U.S. Biopharma Equity Research, told CNBC on Monday, August 24, that the biotech M&A freeze is over. She sees capital markets reopening, large-cap pharma buyers committing to more deals, and fresh oncology data proving that innovation extends well beyond weight-loss drugs.

Why Biotech M&A Suddenly Froze

Field described the prior slowdown in blunt terms. "For a while we had the GLP-1 story, though it felt that that was very company-specific. And then at the beginning of the Trump administration, there were so many questions about broader policy, drug pricing. And so it felt like it put M&A, which really is the lifeblood of the biotech industry, kind of on pause for a while," she said.

She believes we're at a turning point: "We get to 2026, and it feels like the capital markets are open for a lot of biotech companies. We're starting to see more M&A from the large pharma buyers. And then also some real innovation I think has really got markets excited. We had Revolution Medicines' pancreatic cancer data earlier this year. And then just last week, we saw the Phase 3 results for the cancer vaccine from Moderna and Merck," Field said.

Cancer Vaccine Catalyst Behind the Call

Moderna (NASDAQ:MRNA) and Merck (NYSE:MRK) are co-developing intismeran autogene, a personalized mRNA cancer vaccine. Moderna's CEO told investors the program is advancing across "a broad portfolio of nine Phase II and Phase III studies," and that the Phase 3 study in adjuvant melanoma is fully enrolled. The five-year Phase 2b data at ASCO 2026 showed a 49% reduction in risk of recurrence or death with the vaccine plus KEYTRUDA versus KEYTRUDA alone, per Moderna's Q2 press release.

The market reaction was immediate. Moderna jumped 177%, and Merck rose 12.5% on the readout covered by CNBC on August 20. Moderna shares are now at $145.04, up 392.13% year to date. Merck trades at $152.54, up 47.07% year to date, with Keytruda-family sales growing 4% to $8.4 billion in Q2.
